topic.title: Turtle Shape and Color
topic.description: Customises a turtle by changing its shape and color before drawing. Introduces turtle appearance methods for more expressive graphics.

learningNotes.whatILearned: A turtle is an object: it has a shape, a colour and a heading, and you change them by calling methods on it.
learningNotes.challenges: I could not run it here, so the pink turtle and the 45-degree turn are things I read rather than things I saw.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Run it once on a machine with a display, and add one comment saying what the four lines are doing.

engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**0 + 30 + 0 = 30%**

**This file cannot be run here.** It needs `tkinter`, and this
machine has no display and no `tkinter` — so the 40 points for *it runs* are
not ones I can give, and they are not given. The other two bands are judged
by reading the code, carefully, line by line.

There is a bigger point here, and it is worth saying plainly: **`tkinter`
does not exist on Termux either.** These files cannot be run on the phone
this whole system is built around. They are not broken — they are stranded.

**What is right, by reading**

Every call is a real turtle method and the calls are in the right order: `shape('turtle')` draws the turtle as a turtle, `color('pink')` makes it pink, `forward(100)` moves it, `right(45)` turns it. The screen is created and `exitonclick()` is called, so the window stays open — this file does not have the disappearing-window problem.

**What is not**

No comments at all, and no explanation of the difference between moving and turning — which is the idea a reader takes away from a turtle. There is no screen setup either, so the window appears at its default size and position rather than where the program means it to be.

**The one thing to fix first**

One comment, on the line where the two ideas meet:

```python
timmy_the_turtle.right(45)  # Turns the turtle; forward() is what moves it.
```
